title: People who worked the whole year and received the most other pay
question: Among people who worked a full year in fiscal 2026, who received the most pay outside salary and overtime?
finding: 431 people with full-year hours received $50,000 or more in other pay in fiscal 2026, 38 of them $100,000 or more. They are in Police (213), Fire Department (94), Public Health (66) and Retirement System (13); the commonest classes are Sergeant 3 (91), Police Officer 3 (54), Lieutenant 3 (40) and Battalion Chief, Fire Suppress (27). The largest is $304,434 on a salary of $454,815 (Alison Romano, Chf Executive & Investment Ofc (class 1119), Retirement System). 13 of the 431 are at the Retirement System, in its executive and investment classes (Chf Executive & Investment Ofc, Director, Managing Director and Senior Portfolio Manager); 9 of them were paid $50,000 or more in other pay the year before as well. The file does not say what it is or how it is set.
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2026: rows with at least nine-tenths of a full-time year’s paid hours and $50,000 or more in the “other salaries” column, largest first. “The year before” is given where the name is rare enough to follow and the department is the same. Board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out. Titles are printed as the payroll prints them (Dep is deputy, Chf is chief, Asst is assistant, Sprv is supervisor, Ofc is officer, EMT is emergency medical technician).
limits: Because these people worked the whole year, a payout on leaving is unlikely to be the explanation, but a payout of leave can also be taken in service where an agreement allows it, and retention pay, standby pay and assignment premiums are all recorded here. Pay set by an individual contract or by a board, as at the Retirement System, is approved by the body that sets it; the question is what it is tied to. The pay codes would answer that for every row.
